story.title: The Exit Weight
story.logline: A man discovers his shadow is getting heavier every day, until it tries to pull him down permanently.
story.twist: The shadow isn't holding him back; it's the physical weight of every person he ever ignored.
story.ending: Will your shadow let you walk away tomorrow?

scenes.narration: My shadow just tried to choke me on the kitchen floor. It is getting heavier every single day.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, in a dimly lit cramped apartment, gasping on the floor as his shadow stretches abnormally off the wall.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up on frantic face, tilting down to the floor.

scenes.narration: At first, I thought it was just a trick of the evening light. A strange angle from the streetlamp outside.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, standing in the cramped apartment staring nervously at the wall.
scenes.camera: Medium shot, tracking backward as he steps away.

scenes.narration: Then it started pulling downward. Dragging me toward the floor like a lead weight stitched to my heels.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, leaning forward unnaturally as if glued to the floorboards.
scenes.camera: Low angle, emphasizing his struggle against gravity.

scenes.narration: I went to the doctor, but the scale showed nothing. My body is light, but my outline is sinking.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, standing on a clinic scale that reads zero while his shadow pools darkly around his ankles.
scenes.camera: Wide shot, clinical lighting, eerie stillness.

scenes.narration: Last night, the shadow grew hands. It reached out and grabbed my ankles, refusing to let me cross the room.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, looking down in terror as dark silhouette hands wrap around his legs.
scenes.camera: Close-up on feet and the warping floor shadow.

scenes.narration: I finally figured out what it wants. It is keeping score of every time I turned my back.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, staring into a bathroom mirror with tear-filled eyes.

scenes.narration: Every stranger I ignored on the subway. Every friend I walked away from when they needed help.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, remembering past moments flashed darkly within the shadow's silhouette.

scenes.narration: The silhouette is no longer mine. It is made of all the people I pretended I could not see.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, lit by a harsh overhead bulb as the shadow morphs into distinct human shapes.

scenes.narration: Now I cannot lift my feet at all. The floorboards are splintering, and I am sinking into the dark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, sinking ankle-deep into solid wooden flooring as hands pull him down.
scenes.camera: Medium shot, zooming in on his terrified expression.

scenes.narration: My shadow just tried to choke me, and I realized I built the weight myself. Will yours let you walk away?
scenes.visual_prompt: Marcus, 28, messy brown hair, wearing a grey hoodie, completely swallowed by the darkness except for his outstretched hand.
scenes.camera: Top-down bird's-eye view fading to complete black.

caption.hook: Your shadow remembers everyone you forgot.
caption.title: The Exit Weight
caption.caption:
For months, I thought I was just getting tired. But my shadow is sinking into the pavement, pulling me down with a force I can no longer fight. It's not holding me back—it's carrying the exact weight of every soul I ever walked past. 

How much does your past weigh?
